paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the LORD reigns, and no flood changes that. The psalm says He is "robed in majesty" and the world "cannot be moved" (Psalm 93:1). Then the floodwaters rise, the rivers raise their voice, and the seas lift their pounding waves (Psalm 93:3). The writer doesn't pretend the water isn't loud. He just says who is above it.

And here's why that matters to YOU. You're gonna have floods, baker. Bills, bad news, a week that piles up like dishes in the sink. The psalm says "Above the roar of many waters—the mighty breakers of the sea—the LORD on high is majestic" (Psalm 93:4). The roar is real, but the LORD is higher than the roar, and His throne was "established long ago" (Psalm 93:2).

So what do you stand on while the water is loud? His word. The writer says, "Your testimonies are fully confirmed," and that holiness adorns the LORD's house "for all the days to come" (Psalm 93:5). I know a little about waiting in the dark, and I'm telling you, a King who was here before the first wave and will be here after the last one is a King you can trust. So when your waters rise, look UP!
